title: How PersonaPlex answers a phone call
subtitle: Twilio streams the call to a FastAPI server that hears with Deepgram, thinks with GPT-4o-mini and speaks with Edge TTS.

nodes.label: Caller
nodes.detail: A person dials the Twilio number. The same pipeline also runs in a browser over a WebSocket, with no phone line needed.
nodes.tradeoff: Phone audio arrives as 8 kHz mu-law, so it has to be converted before speech to text can use it.

nodes.label: Call webhook
nodes.detail: Twilio posts to /twilio/inbound. The server checks the X-Twilio-Signature header, then replies with TwiML that opens a media stream.
nodes.tradeoff: Requests with a bad signature get a 403, which blocks fake calls but needs the Twilio auth token set.

nodes.label: Media stream
nodes.detail: A FastAPI WebSocket at /twilio/stream receives base64 mu-law audio, decodes it to 16 kHz PCM, and sends replies back down the same socket.
nodes.tradeoff: Listening and answering run as two concurrent asyncio tasks, so the server keeps hearing the caller while the agent talks.

nodes.label: Speech to text
nodes.detail: Streams audio to Deepgram's nova-2 model with interim results and voice activity events. Final pieces are held until Deepgram marks speech_final.
nodes.tradeoff: If speech_final never comes, an UtteranceEnd event after 1,000 ms of silence flushes the text instead.

nodes.label: Persona file
nodes.detail: Each persona (visa consultant, customer service, teacher) is a YAML file that becomes the system prompt and the opening greeting.
nodes.tradeoff: Persona names are checked against a whitelist; an unknown name falls back to the default persona.

nodes.label: LLM
nodes.detail: GPT-4o-mini streams a reply of up to 300 tokens from the call history, with the persona as the system prompt. The README puts the cost at about $0.001 per conversation.
nodes.tradeoff: Trimmed history keeps the system prompt and first two exchanges plus recent turns, so the caller's name isn't forgotten.

nodes.label: Voice tools
nodes.detail: The LLM can call get_weather, which fetches wttr.in, or get_time, which reads the server clock.
nodes.tradeoff: The code runs the tool, but passing its result back into a follow-up reply is still a simplified stub.

nodes.label: Text to speech
nodes.detail: edge-tts speaks the reply in an Indian English neural voice; pydub converts the MP3 to 8 kHz mu-law for the phone line.
nodes.tradeoff: On calls the whole reply is voiced at once; the browser path voices it sentence by sentence as tokens arrive.

nodes.label: Barge-in guard
nodes.detail: Reply audio goes out in 1-second chunks. Before each chunk it checks for a new caller transcript and, if there is one, sends Twilio a clear event.
nodes.tradeoff: Barge-in fires on a finished caller transcript, not raw sound, and is checked once per 1-second chunk.

flow.text: A caller dials the Twilio number.
Checks Twilio's signature and returns TwiML that opens a media stream.
Decodes 8 kHz mu-law audio to 16 kHz PCM and passes it on.
Deepgram transcribes and waits for speech_final before handing the sentence over.
GPT-4o-mini drafts a reply as the visa consultant persona.
Edge TTS voices the reply and pydub converts it for the phone line.
If the caller cuts in, playback stops between 1-second chunks.
Hears the reply, or is listened to again after interrupting.

takeaways.text: Replies wait for Deepgram's speech_final, with a 1,000 ms UtteranceEnd fallback, so the agent doesn't answer mid-sentence.
Playback goes out in 1-second chunks so a new caller transcript can cut the agent off between them.
Trimmed history always keeps the system prompt and first two exchanges, so details from turn one survive.
